text:
maria_sales: Heads-up: medtech procurement wants a 2-week POC that is strictly in-country for Canada + Brazil. SLA ask: 95th <200ms. They also want a complete list of any third parties that will touch data and whether any backups/replication cross borders. Need a quick decision today.

olivia_presales: Do they require both countries active at start, or would a staggered approach (Canada then Brazil) be acceptable to reduce complexity?

samir_sre: Short answer: Canada (ca-central1) hosted can meet latency. Brazil (sa-east1) hosted is available but limited; guaranteeing "country-only" storage requires region-dedicated compute or a Private deployment. Edge nodes can help latency but don't satisfy strict residency because of control-plane/backup flows.

maria_sales: Customer phrased it as "data must not leave national borders" in the security questionnaire. Is hosted effectively out if phrased that way?

anya_security: For PHI-sensitive workloads that wording is binding. Hosted multi-tenant cannot provide an absolute guarantee about copies/replication/metrics leaving the country. Options that meet the language: 1) Temporary Dedicated (region-pinned) per country with replication disabled, or 2) Private (VPC/on-prem). BYOK is good for keys but does not prevent metadata or control-plane info from leaving the country.

ash_ops: I can run quota checks and a quick cost sketch. Need expected model size, avg seq, and peak QPS. Also: do they accept reduced observability (in-country metrics only)?

maria_sales: Model ~7B, avg seq ~512, nightly scan spikes ~35-45 QPS for 20-30m; baseline ~4-6 QPS. They prefer full telemetry but say they can accept limited in-country metrics if needed.

olivia_presales: If we propose a 14-day Dedicated per country, recommend config: 2x A10G-equivalent nodes with tenant pinning and replication disabled. I'll draft a short one-pager comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private.

samir_sre: Example routing snippet we can show their SOC team (for Dedicated):
```json
{"routing": {"mode": "country_lock", "countries": ["CA", "BR"], "replication": "off", "failover": "manual"}, "capacity": {"gpus": 2, "class": "a10g", "term_days": 14}}
```

anya_security: I'll compile a minimal subprocessor manifest: hosted: CSP infra, metrics backend, logs, KMS provider; dedicated: smaller list (CSP infra + KMS if we host). For Private/on-prem the subproc list is essentially the customer's infra. I'll attach SOC2 pointers and PHI checklist. Legal will need to review any contract language about "no copies".

noah_legal: If they insist on contractual "no copies leave country" we need to see the proposed subproc manifest and may need special contract language/attestations. Also note that public CSP SOC reports are fine, but nonpublic auditor contacts require CSP engagement.

ash_ops: Ballpark cost: 2x A10G-equivalent reserved pool for 14 days ~ ~$13k-17k per country (very rough). Hosted per-token cost for expected volume likely materially lower but fails the strict in-country-only constraint. I'll confirm exact numbers after quota check.

maria_sales: Timeline to share with customer?

ash_ops: Today: quota check and rough ballpark. Tonight: security posts subproc manifest draft. Tomorrow AM: firm pricing. Provisioning: ~48-72h after PO + legal/security signoff. Blockers: legal approval on subproc disclosure and budget/PO.

olivia_presales: I'll prepare a short tradeoffs note for the customer (latency vs cost vs residency) and offer Canada-first as an option to reduce risk and cost.

anya_security: FYI: BYOK with an in-country KMS is a strong control but not a substitute for region-pinned storage guarantees. If they accept BYOK + attestations for log/metrics minimization we can consider hosted with strict controls, but otherwise recommend Dedicated/Private.

maria_sales: Perfect. I'll tell them: (1) we can do a short Dedicated pilot to meet the in-country wording, (2) propose Canada-first if they want to reduce timeline/cost, (3) we'll provide subproc list and SOC2 pointers today and a firm price tomorrow. Thanks team :thumbsup:
